questions.key_step: Integrating factor $\sqrt{1+x^2}$ makes the right side $5x^2$.
questions.justification: Routine linear DE with a radical integrating factor; a few standard steps, no insight.

questions.key_step: Differentiate the integral equation to get $xf'=-f$.
questions.justification: One familiar move (Leibniz) then a trivial separable DE; short with options.

questions.key_step: $t=\ln\cos x$ gives integrating factor $t^3$ and an exact right side.
questions.justification: Non-obvious integrating factor ($\ln\cos x$ cubed) with a precise log evaluation at the end; options help.

questions.key_step: Integrate $\frac{2\cos x+1}{(\cos x+2)^2}$ (half-angle substitution or exact quotient derivative) after IF $\sec x$.
questions.justification: Long chain: IF, trig rewrite, tan(x/2) with a hidden $t+3/t$ substitution, then surds; one slip fails.

questions.key_step: Factor the quartic and split into two arctangents.
questions.justification: Routine factorisation plus partial fractions into standard arctans.

questions.key_step: Factor $2xy(x^2+4)$ to see the linear form with factor $x^2+4$.
questions.justification: Standard linear DE with a quick integral; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Differentiate the circle family once and eliminate $g$.
questions.justification: Standard formation of a DE; algebra elimination, no idea needed.

questions.key_step: Recognise $2x\ln x\,y'+2y=2x(y\ln x)'$ and integrate $\ln x/x^2$ by parts.
questions.justification: Linear DE with a log coefficient, by-parts integral and a singular point at $x=1$ to be careful with.

questions.key_step: Substitute $t=\tan^{-1}x$ to get $y_t+y=e^t$.
questions.justification: Standard substitution then a linear DE; short and routine.

questions.key_step: Group into $d(xy)$, $d(y^2)$, $d(x^2)$, then circle conditions $\beta=0$, equal coefficients.
questions.justification: Two ideas linked (exact grouping and circle conditions); the denominator is disguised.

questions.key_step: $t=e^{\tan x}$ turns the right side into $\frac{dt}{1+t^2}$.
questions.justification: Separable with one substitution and an arctan identity at the end; routine.

questions.key_step: Differentiate the area to get $f$; eliminate both constants by $y''/y'=f''/f'$.
questions.justification: Two linked ideas (area to function, formation of a second-order DE) with sign care in the options.

questions.key_step: Multiply by $\sec y$ to get a linear equation in $\tan y$, then $\int x^3e^{x^2}dx$.
questions.justification: One recognised reduction then a linear DE and a by-parts integral; routine.

questions.key_step: Integrate term by term and read off the vertex of the parabola.
questions.justification: Direct integration plus completing the square; routine.

questions.key_step: Homogeneous equation: $y=vx$, separate, then simplify the logs.
questions.justification: Standard homogeneous method; moderately long algebra with options to match.

questions.key_step: Differentiate to $y'^2+y^2=1$, pick the branch $y=\sin x$ with $y\ge0$.
questions.justification: Two ideas (Leibniz, then branch selection with $y\ge0$) and the singular constant solution is a trap.

questions.key_step: Both solutions are exponentials; $e^{a-b}=\frac43$ gives $t$.
questions.justification: One familiar move (exponential solutions) then log algebra.

questions.key_step: Separate with partial fractions, then use 'slope never zero' to fix the sign inside the modulus.
questions.justification: Partial fractions on both sides and a subtle range argument for the modulus.

questions.key_step: Integrating factor $1+\cos^2x$ since $d(1+\cos^2x)=-\sin2x\,dx$.
questions.justification: Standard linear DE with a trig integrating factor; short.

questions.key_step: $xy'-y=x^2(y/x)'$ so $t=y/x$ gives $\cos t\,dt=dx/x$.
questions.justification: Standard homogeneous-type substitution; short chain.
